flawed_step: Step 2: the claim that every finite unit-distance graph has a vertex of degree at most 2 is false.
assessment_summary:
1. [JUSTIFIED] Let G be an arbitrary finite unit-distance graph; proving that G is 3-colorable would establish the first clause.
2. [NOT JUSTIFIED] Assert that every nonempty induced subgraph of G has a vertex of degree at most 2. This does not follow from the definition and is false: the graph consisting of the center and six vertices of a regular unit hexagon has minimum degree 3.
3. [NOT JUSTIFIED] Repeatedly remove a vertex of degree at most 2 to obtain a 2-degeneracy ordering. This would follow from Step 2, but Step 2 is false, so the ordering is not established.
4. [NOT JUSTIFIED] Color vertices in reverse removal order, assigning each one a color different from its at most two colored neighbors. This greedy procedure is conditionally sound, but its required ordering was not established in Step 3.
5. [NOT JUSTIFIED] Conclude that every unit-distance graph is 3-colorable. The conclusion rests on the failed Step 2.
6. [JUSTIFIED] To determine whether this is merely a proof gap, define the seven points x,y,z,a,b,c,d listed in counterexample.
7. [JUSTIFIED] Direct calculation gives |x-a|=|x-b|=|y-a|=|y-b|=|a-b|=1: for example, |x-a|²=3/4+1/4=1, and the other equalities follow similarly.
8. [JUSTIFIED] Also |x-c|=|x-d|=|z-c|=|z-d|=|c-d|=1. Indeed, |z|=√3, while c and d equal z/2 plus or minus a perpendicular vector of length 1/2, so each is one unit from both x and z and they are one unit apart.
9. [JUSTIFIED] Finally, |y-z|²=(√3/6)²+(√33/6)²=1, so yz is an edge.
10. [JUSTIFIED] In any proper 3-coloring, the triangle xab uses all three colors because xa, xb, and ab are edges.
11. [JUSTIFIED] Since y is adjacent to both a and b, it must receive the remaining color, namely the color of x.
12. [JUSTIFIED] Applying the same reasoning to the triangle xcd and the vertex z shows that z must also receive the color of x.
13. [JUSTIFIED] Steps 11–12 give y and z the same color, contradicting the edge yz from Step 9.
14. [JUSTIFIED] Thus this finite unit-distance graph is not 3-colorable, so the statement is false; consequently its asserted conclusion about the plane does not follow.
